story.headline: Spain crash toll rises to 69
story.summary: The death toll from the high-speed train collision near Urda, in Spain's Toledo province, on Wednesday 28 October has risen to 69, with 58 injured, and the government says human error in handling a signalling failure caused it.
story.display_body: The death toll from the high-speed train collision near Urda, in Spain's Toledo province, on Wednesday 28 October has risen to 69, with 58 injured, and the government says human error in handling a signalling failure caused it.
story.why: the government's account puts the blame on a human decision made after an automatic safeguard failed, not on the hardware. That raises the question of why a known fallback procedure allowed full-speed running, and it comes during Spain's campaign for the general election on 29 November.

story.headline: Russian drone hits train at Dnipro station
story.summary: A Russian jet-powered drone struck a passenger train standing at Dnipro railway station on the morning of Thursday 29 October, killing at least 13 people and wounding at least five, Ukrainian authorities said.
story.display_body: A Russian jet-powered drone struck a passenger train standing at Dnipro railway station on the morning of Thursday 29 October, killing at least 13 people and wounding at least five, Ukrainian authorities said. The train was about to leave for Zaporizhzhia. Ukrainian Railways said people had stayed on the platform despite an air-raid alert and warnings of a heightened threat. Dnipropetrovsk governor Oleksandr Hanzha said medics were treating casualties at the scene. The strike follows a Russian campaign against Ukraine's railways that has increasingly hit passenger trains.

story.headline: Ship ablaze in Strait of Hormuz
story.summary: A ship was reported on fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday 29 October, about 9 nautical miles north of Khasab in Oman, the British navy-run UKMTO maritime agency said.
story.display_body: A ship was reported on fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday 29 October, about 9 nautical miles north of Khasab in Oman, the British navy-run UKMTO maritime agency said. UKMTO gave no cause and no information about the crew. On the same day, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three tankers had exploded and caught fire over the past 24 hours after hitting sea mines while using an "unauthorized" route. It is not known whether the burning ship is one of them, and the Guards' claims, including that they downed another US drone east of the strait, have not been independently verified. A US-based think tank, the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, says attacks on shipping are at their highest level since the US–Israeli strikes on Iran in February began the war. Donald Trump said last week "we may do another little Epic Fury", referring to those strikes, without giving a timeframe. Meanwhile a third US aircraft carrier is heading to the region.
story.why: Switzerland's fuel supply is already strained (see below). A new round of strikes after the US midterms on Tuesday 3 November would put more pressure on the oil route that has disrupted fuel supplies since February.

story.headline: North Korea fires ten ballistic missiles
story.summary: North Korea fired about ten short-range ballistic missiles into the sea off its east coast from near Wonsan at around 12:30 local time on Thursday 29 October, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said.
story.display_body: North Korea fired about ten short-range ballistic missiles into the sea off its east coast from near Wonsan at around 12:30 local time on Thursday 29 October, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said. Japan said they landed outside its exclusive economic zone. It is Pyongyang's latest of more than ten launch rounds this year; the previous one was on 12 October. The launch comes during a row over landmines that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone on 21 September. A joint South Korean–UN investigation concluded this month that the North had planted them south of the demarcation line. Pyongyang denies it and has rejected Seoul's demand for an apology. Seoul has proposed talks to clarify the border, and the North has not replied.

story.headline: US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry
story.summary: The US Treasury on Wednesday 28 October sanctioned Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and the Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a financial institution for members of the security forces, over Rwanda's support for the M23 rebels in eastern DR Congo.
story.display_body: The US Treasury on Wednesday 28 October sanctioned Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and the Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a financial institution for members of the security forces, over Rwanda's support for the M23 rebels in eastern DR Congo. "Rwanda must end its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. This comes a few months after Washington sanctioned the Rwandan army.

story.headline: Cuba embargo vote hits 20-year low
story.summary: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday 28 October called for the 34th time for an end to the US embargo on Cuba, but with its weakest backing in two decades: 130 votes in favour, 17 against and 25 abstentions.
story.display_body: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday 28 October called for the 34th time for an end to the US embargo on Cuba, but with its weakest backing in two decades: 130 votes in favour, 17 against and 25 abstentions. Last year the resolution passed 165–7 with 12 abstentions. UN News notes that Cuba is in a severe energy crisis, made worse by a US fuel embargo imposed after what it calls "the rendition of Venezuela's president to New York". The resolution is not binding.

story.headline: Nuclear ban repeal goes to February vote
story.summary: The Federal Council on Wednesday 28 October set five items for the federal vote of Sunday 28 February 2027, including the amendment to the Nuclear Energy Act that lifts the ban on new nuclear plants.
story.display_body: The Federal Council on Wednesday 28 October set five items for the federal vote of Sunday 28 February 2027, including the amendment to the Nuclear Energy Act that lifts the ban on new nuclear plants. The nuclear amendment, which Parliament adopted on 19 June 2026, is the indirect counter-proposal to the "Blackout stoppen" initiative, and it would reverse the new-build ban voters approved in 2017. Voters will also decide on a law change that lets national collective labour agreements with minimum wages below cantonal minimum wages be declared generally binding, on the EFTA–Malaysia economic partnership agreement, on the "foie gras" import-ban initiative, and on the "democracy initiative" for a modernised citizenship law.
story.why: the nuclear and minimum-wage items each settle a long-running Swiss fight, over energy policy and over whether cantonal wage floors can be overridden by national agreements.

story.headline: Bern weighs 80 km/h motorway limit
story.summary: The federal office for economic supply is considering an 80 km/h limit on motorways in case Switzerland's fuel shortage worsens, its delegate Roland Pfister told SRF on Thursday 29 October, but says the measure is far from being used.
story.display_body: The federal office for economic supply is considering an 80 km/h limit on motorways in case Switzerland's fuel shortage worsens, its delegate Roland Pfister told SRF on Thursday 29 October, but says the measure is far from being used. The supply is tight because of the Middle East war and the long-running low water on the Rhine, which has sharply cut the barge traffic that normally brings petrol and heating oil from Rotterdam to Basel. Fuel still arrives by rail from Germany and as crude oil piped from Marseille to the Cressier refinery (NE). Pfister said a serious shortage would come only if a pipeline were damaged for several weeks; heavy rain in southern France briefly cut one last week. Since September the federal government has drawn lightly on compulsory stocks; last week it released 4% of diesel stocks. The 80 km/h limit would come only after a substantial share of reserves had been used and voluntary saving had failed. Pfister says the Federal Council could impose it quickly, and that it would both save fuel and send "a very strong signal".
entities: Federal Office for National Economic Supply

story.headline: Israeli or French system for air defence
story.summary: The Federal Council on Wednesday 28 October shortlisted Israel's Barak MX and France's SAMP/T NG for a second long-range air-defence system, and decided to keep the US Patriot order despite delivery delays.
story.display_body: The Federal Council on Wednesday 28 October shortlisted Israel's Barak MX and France's SAMP/T NG for a second long-range air-defence system, and decided to keep the US Patriot order despite delivery delays. Four manufacturers, from France, Israel and South Korea, had bid. The defence department must now weigh foreign-policy and economic factors alongside military ones. Washington has given Patriot delivery priority to countries that gave their own systems to Ukraine. The government says dropping Patriot without a replacement is "not an option". In the winter session, Parliament is due to debate a 24-billion-franc increase in army funding that includes 6 billion for the second system and part of Patriot's extra costs. A decision is expected in early 2027.
story.why: an Israeli system is one of the two left in the running, which makes the choice a political test as well as a technical one for a neutral country.

story.headline: Switzerland to adopt EU return rules
story.summary: The Federal Council on Wednesday 28 October approved taking over the EU's new Return Regulation as a Schengen development, subject to Swiss approval procedures, with a consultation on the necessary law changes due at the end of January 2027.
story.display_body: The Federal Council on Wednesday 28 October approved taking over the EU's new Return Regulation as a Schengen development, subject to Swiss approval procedures, with a consultation on the necessary law changes due at the end of January 2027. The regulation lets a Schengen state enforce another state's removal decision and allows people ordered to leave to be transferred by force to a non-EU country where they have a right to stay, or to which a return agreement applies, if human rights and non-refoulement (the ban on sending people where they face serious harm) are respected. It also allows "return hubs" outside the Schengen area. Maximum detention pending removal rises from six to twelve months, extendable to 24, and entry bans of up to ten years become possible. As a Schengen associate, Switzerland must adopt binding Schengen developments.

story.headline: Federal books swing to a surplus
story.summary: The Confederation now expects a 2026 financing surplus of 0.7 billion francs instead of the budgeted 0.7 billion deficit, according to the second extrapolation the Federal Council published on Wednesday 28 October.
story.display_body: The Confederation now expects a 2026 financing surplus of 0.7 billion francs instead of the budgeted 0.7 billion deficit, according to the second extrapolation the Federal Council published on Wednesday 28 October. The improvement of about 1.5 billion comes mainly from profit-tax receipts, revised up by 0.5 billion, while withholding-tax receipts were revised down by 0.8 billion because refunds for 2023 are running well above the provision. Receipts from the new OECD minimum-tax top-up arrive for the first time this year, but no reliable estimate is possible yet.
story.why: the surplus comes as the 2027 budget-relief programme cuts federal spending, for example by ending general-budget top-ups for building-renovation subsidies. That puts the argument that cuts are urgent under closer scrutiny.

story.headline: Cassis reopens Swiss office in Pyongyang
story.summary: Foreign minister Ignazio Cassis is visiting North Korea on Thursday 29 and Friday 30 October to attend the official reopening of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang 23 years after Micheline Calmy-Rey's visit.
story.display_body: Foreign minister Ignazio Cassis is visiting North Korea on Thursday 29 and Friday 30 October to attend the official reopening of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang 23 years after Micheline Calmy-Rey's visit. The office is attached to the embassy in Beijing. It closed in 2020 during the pandemic and has been operating again since 19 October. "In a period of strong geopolitical tension we need more channels of communication, not fewer," foreign-ministry spokesman Nicolas Bideau told Le Temps.

story.headline: Bern opposes alternating-custody bill
story.summary: The Federal Council on Wednesday 28 October advised Parliament not to take up a National Council committee bill that would favour alternating custody after separation, even in disputed cases, where it best serves the child.
story.display_body: The Federal Council on Wednesday 28 October advised Parliament not to take up a National Council committee bill that would favour alternating custody after separation, even in disputed cases, where it best serves the child. It says current law, under which courts must examine alternating custody whenever one parent asks for it, together with Federal Supreme Court case law, is sufficient. The bill implements parliamentary initiative 21.449 (Kamerzin).
